newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin says no changes regarding Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin says no changes regarding Yeltsin.

text.p: The Kremlin, clearly exasperated by rumours on financial markets about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, said on Tuesday that nothing had changed regarding the president.

"We do not comment on market rumours," a press spokesman said. "That's what my bosses have told me to say... It is a game and we do not want to be players. Someone is trying to a make lot of money on this by spreading such rumours."
Asked repeatedly where Yeltsin was, the spokesman replied: "He is where he was. Please refer to what the press secretary said as to what he is doing."

Press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing on Monday that Yeltsin was leaving hospital after treatment for pneumonia and he would be working on documents at the official Gorky-9 residence outside Moscow.

Financial traders outside Russia reported scattered market rumours that Yeltsin was either dead or very ill and said the talk was affecting international bond futures markets. It was unclear where the talk originated.
